obtained.how: the two routes the entry names, queried 2026-11-26. (1) MDIFW's ArcGIS Online services for the 2nd Maine Bird Atlas (services1.arcgis.com/RbMX0mRVOFNTdLzd): BirdAtlas_BAEA_BlockCodes, BirdAtlas_GBHE_BlockCodes, MEIFW_BirdAtlasBlockCompletion, WinterAtlasResults (layer 0 of each), every block within about 25 km of the lakes, with the layers' renderer labels. (2) The GBIF occurrence API for the regional box 45.50–45.80° N, 67.75–68.10° W (bald eagle, common loon, belted kingfisher, American bittern, osprey, hooded merganser, great blue heron). Raw JSON saved as MaineBirdAtlas_.<layer>.json and MaineBirdAtlas_.gbif_*.json; attribute rows and records dumped, without coordinates, to MaineBirdAtlas_.gis.txt. The README of DigitalMaine's 'Breeding Bird Evidence Summary, Maine Bird Atlas 2 (2018–2022)' package was also read

bibliography.checked_against: the services' descriptions and copyright lines; DigitalMaine's record and README; GBIF's dataset record
bibliography.corrections: Name the parts. (a) The atlas: Maine Bird Atlas 2 (2018–2022), Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife. Its block results are served by MDIFW's ArcGIS Online services BirdAtlas_BAEA_BlockCodes ('Species block codes for Bald Eagle from the 2nd Maine Bird Atlas 2018-2022'), BirdAtlas_GBHE_BlockCodes, MEIFW_BirdAtlasBlockCompletion and WinterAtlasResults, all © MDIFW, at https://services1.arcgis.com/RbMX0mRVOFNTdLzd/ArcGIS/rest/services/. The full table is DigitalMaine's 'Breeding Bird Evidence Summary, Maine Bird Atlas 2 (2018–2022)' (2022), https://digitalmaine.com/maine_bird_atlas_visualization_shapefiles/1. Cite with the access date. (b) The GBIF records are not atlas records. All but two of those used are from 'EOD – eBird Observation Dataset' (Cornell Lab of Ornithology, doi:10.15468/aomfnb, accessed via GBIF 26 Nov 2026), so cite them as eBird via GBIF.

claims.claim: eagles were at the Upper nest in July 2018 (credited to MDIFW's records; lead: is it a Maine Bird Atlas record?)
claims.source_value: GBIF holds one eBird record (EOD dataset, Cornell Lab of Ornithology) of 1 bald eagle on 20 July 2018 at a point at the Upper nest site [location withheld]. The record has no breeding code, behaviour or nest remark, and it is not labelled an atlas record. The eBird checklist page is behind a bot check. The atlas layers give only each block's highest breeding code, not dated sightings
claims.location: web page (GBIF occurrence API), EOD – eBird Observation Dataset, record of 2018-07-20 [record and checklist IDs withheld; in the git-ignored MaineBirdAtlas_.gbif_baea.json]
claims.quote: Bald Eagle | eventDate: 2018-07-20 | individualCount: 1 | dataset: eBird
claims.conditions: one eBird checklist (two observers listed) in 2018, the atlas's first season; one bird
claims.note: Rewrite as 'an eagle was recorded at the nest site on 20 July 2018 (eBird, via GBIF)'. Use 'an eagle' (individualCount 1), and do not say 'at the nest' in the sense of nesting, which the record does not show. MDIFW's nest layers stop at 2013 (see MDIFW_nd-2). It may be the checklist behind the block's 'confirmed' code, but GBIF cannot show that.

claims.claim: the hooded merganser records include July broods
claims.note: The 9 GBIF records include three July 2021 eBird records of 3 birds each (two at one location on 20 and 27 July, one at another on 26 July). No record carries an age, sex or breeding code, so 'broods' is an inference from group size and date. The atlas's species-by-block table (which would hold FL/FY codes) is behind a bot check. Say 'groups of three in July' or drop 'with July broods'.

claims.claim: two loons were recorded on 27 May 2022, very probably on Lower
claims.source_value: eBird record (via GBIF): 2 common loons, 27 May 2022, at a point on land about 0.6 km from Lower's shore and 1.7 km from Upper's
claims.location: web page (GBIF occurrence API), EOD – eBird Observation Dataset, common loon records of 2022 [record ID withheld]
claims.quote: Common Loon | eventDate: 2022-05-27 | individualCount: 2 | dataset: eBird
claims.conditions: distances are project arithmetic from the record's point to the lake outlines in tools/hotbrook/data
claims.note: 'Very probably on Lower' is an inference from the point's position, nearer Lower than Upper. eBird points often mark a checklist's place loosely. It is an eBird record, not an atlas record.

notes: Answer to the lead: the July 2018 eagle is in eBird (via GBIF), not in any MDIFW layer and not visibly in the atlas data. It is one bird on 20 July 2018 at a point at the Upper nest site, with no nesting behaviour recorded. The atlas's block data confirm breeding in a block covering part of Upper and support the other atlas claims. The hooded-merganser 'broods' are not in the records. For the human: the DigitalMaine attribute table (Breeding Bird Evidence Summary, 27.8 MB DBF) opens in a browser and would give every species' code in the four lake blocks (loon, osprey, hooded and common merganser, kingfisher). The DigitalMaine README codes 0 = not observed, 1 = observed, 2 = possible, 3 = probable, 4 = confirmed; the MDIFW services code missing values 'NA' = 'No data'.
